findings.description: docs/payments.md states that refund limits are configured per merchant and enforced before funds are released, but refund() carries only a TODO for that check and never calls RefundPolicy.isRefundAllowed or loadRefundPolicy. Worse, RefundPolicy reads a single global PAYMENT_REFUND_LIMIT from the environment rather than a per-merchant configuration, so even the unimplemented check would not be per-merchant.

findings.whyItMatters: A support agent (or a compromised agent session) can refund arbitrary amounts above the merchant's contracted ceiling, and funds are marked released before the daily reconciliation sees them.
consequences: Refunds exceeding the merchant's configured limit are accepted and recorded
The documented guarantee to merchants is false
No audit-worthy rejection exists for over-limit requests
Over-limit damage is only discovered at the next daily reconciliation
findings.reproduction: POST /api/payments/:id/refund with amountCents just below the payment amount on a merchant whose admin-console limit is far lower; the request returns 202 with no limit error.
findings.recommendation: Load the merchant's policy before mutating anything and call isRefundAllowed(payment, requestedCents, policy) (cumulative against total_refunded, not just the single request); reject over-limit requests with a ValidationError before recordRefund/update. Replace the global env override with a per-merchant lookup.
findings.reasoning: The refund path moves money and records the refund without consulting any limit; RefundPolicy is dead code that nothing imports on the refund path. The requirement text explicitly promises enforcement before release.
